recipes.name: Garbage Plate Sauce
ingredients_raw: 1.25 cups water, plus more as needed

steps.text: Cook ground beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat until browned and crumbly, 5 to 7 minutes. Drain and discard grease.
Transfer cooked beef to a blender and process until finely minced.

Return minced, cooked beef to the skillet. Add 1 1/4 cups water, vinegar, paprika, black pepper, chili powder, cayenne pepper, salt, allspice, cloves, cumin, thyme, and cinnamon. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then cook for at least 30 minutes, adding water as needed to keep the mixture moist and gravy-like.

raw_recipe.headline: Garbage Plate Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Garbage plate sauce hails from Rochester, New York. This deliciously seasoned meat sauce is usually poured over macaroni salad or home fries.

review.reviewBody: Mrs Jones must be a Rochester, NY native. All the right ingredients, I just like mine with a lot more chili powder and cayenne. Personal thing. I also add a 1/2 cup of beef broth in place of water initially.

I just got done making this. I am a Rochester native but also a vegetarian so I've always gotten the grilled cheese garbage plate without the meat hot sauce. I made this for me and my husband with veggie burgers and I used tofu crumbled up for the hot sauce. They came out great! My (non-vegetarian) husband said they tasted just like Nick Tahou's! I didn't have the allspice or thyme but the hot sauce was delicious!! To make it with the tofu I squeezed out the excess water and baked the tofu at 375 for about 25 minutes to get rid of some of the water. Then I simmered the tofu adding a little oil and all the ingredients and then added water until it was the right consistency. You really can't taste the tofu (and what a healthy alternative!). This sauce was really great and the garbage plates hit the spot!

Not bad. Just a couple of things to point out.

1) double the meat or halve the spices.
2) needs tomato paste, about 4 oz/ lb of ground beef.
3) could leave the vinegar out.
4) really no need to blend the beef, just keep chopping it with a spatula and fry it till it's krispy.
5) sautéed onions in the sauce as well.

Binging with Babbish did a really good cover of a garbage plate. Recipe is very similar with the exceptions that I noted.

The recipe is great! I made some substitutions, but the recipe as written works well, too. If you want to amp it up, make these changes: replace the vinegar with Frank's red hot sauce, add 2 tbsp. tomato paste, 1 tsp garlic powder, and replace the water with beef stock/broth. This was good for 4 plates but I'd still double it next time!

I love this! So flavourful and so fast. The only things I do differently is to make it with Beyond Beef and to skip the blender step. 

Measuring out all the spices can be a little fiddly, so I've made up a large batch of the spice mix to keep in the cupboard (1 generous tablespoon/4 servings). It's as easy as making Hamburger Helper, but far more delicious. I'd like to try using this mix with a lentil base next.

12.24.13 - In an effort to replicate another Rochester joint's flavor (Charlie Riedel's), I followed my brother's advice and made the following changes:

Made it with vegetarian "beef" crumbles so that DBF could partake
Left out cloves and cinnamon
Added a tiny bit of olive oil with the "beef"
Did NOT stick the "beef" in a blender

Next time, I may cut back on the black pepper a little and leave out the cumin.

02.02.14 - Made this for party, doubled recipe (still vegetarian), kept other mods and halved black pepper and cumin.

05.02.14 - No cumin, cinnamon, or cloves. Halve the black pepper. Add a little bit of olive oil (for veggie ground).

Don't use the amount of ground cloves listed, it completely overpowers the rest of the spices and makes it inedible. 
I discarded mine and started over.
Adjusting the recipe for one pound of ground beef, I added just 1/8 tsp. of cloves and it was fine.

From Rochester and this is great! Doubled the recipe and left the burger grease in it (since it’s a garbage plate after all) and added about a teaspoon of red pepper flakes and about 3tbsp of hot sauce (tapatio is my favorite for some slow heat) and it still wasn’t too spicy. I ended up making plates for about 20 with the double recipe and I didn’t even get to eat one since they got gobbled up. I tasted the sauce though and it was fantastic!

There aren't many hots places around Rochester that I haven't tried. This recipe yields an excellent hot sauce, better than the more commonly found recipes out there. I added a touch of beef broth like someone here recommended, and at the end threw in a few dashes of red hot, but that's it. A hand blender works well for fine grinding the whole thing once it's simmered. Definitely developed more flavor after ~1 hr on low. Thanks for a winner!

I loved garbage plates when I went to college at RIT years ago, and dearly missed them after moving away from Rochester. I eventually came across this recipe, making it with lots of cautious excitement. Smelling those nostalgic smells while it bubbling away on the stove brought a huge smile to my face, and I was overwhelmed with happiness when eating it on my first homemade garbage plate. I've made this recipe again and again since then. I typically quadruple the batch, making the measurements easier (remember that 4 TBSP of vinegar = 1/4 cup!). Thank you so much for this!!!

I've made this recipe with some of my own tweaks which I cannot really mention here, but as it is the recipe is fantastic. I've worked for years making this recipe to get a combination I like that I can scale up to use with 2.5 pounds of meat. I think it needs more chili powder, more cayenne, more black pepper, and one or two secrets. I do put a tiny bit of tomato paste in. Some Rochester sauces have tomato some do not. I put the smallest amount in. Another ingredient I basically put in there to throw people off when they see it. It's like if they tried to copy my recipe and saw little things in there they'd think it needed it, but it kind of doesn't. I'm sure it lends a slight flavor to my sauce, but it's not required. As for the person that said something about not blending the beef.. they're wrong. Do not fry until crispy. You don't want it crispy. Also, you don't have to blend it.. you can just mix it with water and the beef will break apart. Someone mentioned simmering this for 30 minutes. Definitely minimum 30 minutes. I usually go longer. Someone mentioned this sounds like Cincinnati chili without the chocolate. Cincinnati chili doesn't usually have chocolate. Skyline does not have chocolate. "The Authentic History of Cincinnati Chili" book states there's no chocolate. Anyway, I made this recipe as is and I've been making it with tweaks for MANY years. I've probably made this 100 times with tweaks.
Meh. Too much cloves.
2x paprika .25x cinnamon best version yet. i am a rochester native and visit yearly and know how it is supposed to taste.
I moved to Arizona and I was craving a garbage plate so I made them at home and used this recipe. This was SPOT ON. Ty so much
I’m from Penfield, New York and this brought me back to my late teens/20’s late night drunk food! Now I make it for my family.

Very good. Make ahead, refrigerate and remove half the solidified grease. 2nd time: did not blend and turned out great. Like the way browning adds to flavor. Might halve the cayenne for people who don't like too much spice. Might add onion powder. Maybe more paprika and a little more cinnamon. I liked this one best.

I was one of the college kids who ate this after the bars - about 30 years ago. And then as a professional engineer - Friday lunch. There were SO MANY different "plates" - fish, egg, hamburger, hot dog, pork chop etc... I lived out West for 10 years and made a similar knock off sauce occasionally. My 59th BDay is coming up, and this is what I'm making for the extended family!
My dad from Rochester said it smelt just like garbage plate and loved it!!!
I think this sounds like Cincinnati Recipe Style Chili just without the chocolate and tomato paste.
Excellent-just added a touch of brown sugar. Need to double all amounts. It freezes well
